existing_coverage: The only supplied test class is src/test/java/com/redhat/lightwell/service/TransactionServiceTest.java, a pure Mockito unit test (@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)) with mocked AccountRepository, TransactionRepository, and AuditService, constructing Customer/Account instances in-memory (no database, no seeded IDs — findById(1L)/findById(2L) are stubbed with locally built objects). It covers: (1) deposit happy path — 500.00 into a 1000.00 account, asserts response amount and balanceAfter=1500.00; (2) withdraw happy path — 300.00 from 1000.00, asserts balanceAfter=700.00; (3) withdraw overdraw — 2000.00 from 1000.00 throws InsufficientFundsException; (4) transfer happy path for a PARTIAL amount only — 200.00 from a 1000.00 source (1L) to a 500.00 target (2L), asserting only the response fields (amount=200.00, source-side balanceAfter=800.00) and never the target account's resulting balance nor the balances passed to accountRepository.save; (5) same-account transfer rejected with IllegalArgumentException. The transfer-side insufficient-funds branch (amount > balance in transfer()) and, critically, the amount == balance boundary are not exercised anywhere.
gap: The exact-full-balance transfer boundary has zero coverage. In TransactionService.transfer the funds check is `if (source.getBalance().compareTo(request.getAmount()) < 0)`, so an amount exactly equal to the available balance (compareTo == 0) is accepted, and the code then computes sourceNewBalance = balance.subtract(amount) (should be exactly 0.00) and targetNewBalance = balance.add(amount), persisting both via accountRepository.save. No supplied test transfers the entire balance: shouldTransferSuccessfully moves only 200.00 of the 1000.00 balance and checks only the source-side response balanceAfter, and the insufficient-funds test covers only the withdraw path with amount > balance. Nothing asserts that the source ends at exactly 0.00, that the target receives the identical amount, or that total funds are conserved (no money lost or created). Per the objective, the smaller-transfer and insufficient-funds tests must not be counted as covering this boundary. A hidden defect that rejects a full-balance transfer as insufficient funds (e.g., guard treating equals as overdraw) or that produces source/target balances other than 0.00 / original+amount would pass the current suite. The needed test: transfer the full available balance between two distinct locally constructed accounts, wrap the service call in JUnit assertDoesNotThrow so an unexpected exception becomes an assertion failure, and assert successful completion with response amount equal to the full balance, response balanceAfter == 0.00, source account balance == 0.00, and target account balance == its original balance plus the transferred amount (fund conservation), using an ArgumentCaptor on accountRepository.save or the mutated in-memory account instances.
